A 437 /// task-level preflight does not change this — the gated dependency edge is drawn exactly like 438 /// any other; the preflight is only ever a check node inside the consumer's own container 439 /// (emitted before the container's guardrail check nodes — see ). 440 /// 441 private static void AppendContainerEdges( 442 DependencyGraph graph, 443 IReadOnlyList tasks, 444 IReadOnlyDictionary nodeIdBase, 445 StringBuilder sb) 446 { 447 foreach (TaskNode root in tasks.Where(t => t.DependsOn.Count == 0)) 448 { 449 AppendLf(sb, $" {PlanPreflightsId} --> task_{nodeIdBase[root.Id]}"); 450 } 451 452 foreach (TaskNode dependency in tasks) 453 { 454 foreach (string dependentId in graph.DependentsOf(dependency.Id) 455 .OrderBy(id => id, StringComparer.Ordinal)) 456 { 457 AppendLf(sb, $" task_{nodeIdBase[dependency.Id]} --> task_{nodeIdBase[dependentId]}"); 458 } 459 } 460 461 foreach (TaskNode leaf in tasks.Where(t => graph.DependentsOf(t.Id).Count == 0)) 462 { 463 AppendLf(sb, $" task_{nodeIdBase[leaf.Id]} --> {PlanGuardrailsId}"); 464 } 465 } 466 467 /// 468 /// Append click directives (HTML-viewer only; see ) for 469 /// every CHECK node — plan-level or task-level, preflight or guardrail — opening its own file 470 /// as a plan-relative, forward-slash file:// target resolved relative to 471 /// diagram.html at the plan root, opened in a new tab (_blank) so the diagram 472 /// stays put. Emitted in the same ordinal/sorted order as the nodes for determinism, and using 473 /// the SAME node-id scheme as so every click target actually 474 /// exists. A task-level preflight's click tooltip carries its FULL description (not just its 475 /// name) since draws only a truncated label for it — the 476 /// tooltip is the click-for-detail mechanism that keeps the full text from being lost. 477 /// 478 /// 479 /// No container click directive is emitted here (issue #235). A task container's click 480 /// target is no longer a Mermaid mechanism at all — see class remarks, "A task container's click 481 /// target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...". injects it via 482 /// JavaScript after Mermaid's render completes, using for the 483 /// folder path data. The tooltip is ALWAYS 511 /// Description ?? Name in full, for every check kind at both scopes — since the drawn 512 /// label is now always the short Name (issue #222), the tooltip is the one place the 513 /// full description lives; there is no longer a "some checks get the full text, others don't" 514 /// distinction. 515 /// 516 private static void AppendCheckClicks( 517 PlanDefinition plan, 518 IReadOnlyList checks, 519 string nodeIdPrefix, 520 StringBuilder sb) 521 { 522 int ordinal = 0; 523 foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal)) 524 { 525 string checkPath = ToPlanRelative(plan.PlanDirectory, check.Path); 526 string tooltipText = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(check.Description) ? check.Name : check.Description!; 527 AppendLf(sb, $" click {nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal} href \"{checkPath}\" \"{ClickTooltip(tooltipText)}\" _blank"); 528 ordinal++; 529 } 530 } 531 532 /// 533 /// A plan-folder-relative, forward-slash path for a click href target. Used everywhere a 558 /// line is emitted INSTEAD of , whose 559 /// Environment.NewLine would inject CRLF on Windows and make the rendered diagram 560 /// (and its source hash) platform-dependent (issue #3). 561 /// 562 private static void AppendLf(StringBuilder sb, string line) => sb.Append(line).Append('\n'); 563 564 // --- node id helpers -------------------------------------------------------------- 565 566 /// 567 /// Build the task-id → node-id-base map for (already ordinal), 568 /// guaranteeing distinct bases even when two task ids to the same 569 /// string (e.g. a.b and a_b both → a_b). The first claimant keeps the 570 /// readable sanitized base; later collisions get a deterministic _2, _3, … 571 /// suffix in ordinal order. Every node/container family for a task (the container itself and 572 /// its preflight/guardrail check nodes) derives from this unique base, so all ids stay 573 /// collision-free. Also used by so its JSON side-table is keyed 574 /// by the SAME container id this method produces for . 575 /// 576 private static IReadOnlyDictionary AllocateNodeIdBases(IReadOnlyList tasks) 577 { 578 var bases = new Dictionary(StringComparer.Ordinal); 579 var taken = new HashSet(StringComparer.Ordinal); 580 581 foreach (TaskNode task in tasks) 582 { 583 string candidate = Sanitize(task.Id); 584 if (!taken.Add(candidate)) 585 { 586 int suffix = 2; 587 string disambiguated; 588 do 589 { 590 disambiguated = $"{candidate}_{suffix}"; 591 suffix++; 592 } 593 while (!taken.Add(disambiguated)); 594 595 candidate = disambiguated; 596 } 597 598 bases[task.Id] = candidate; 599 } 600 601 return bases; 602 } 603 604 /// 605 /// Turn an id into a safe Mermaid node-id fragment: every character that is not an ASCII 606 /// letter, digit, or underscore becomes _ (so kebab - → _). Because 607 /// this is many-to-one (e.g. a.b and a_b both map to a_b), 608 /// deduplicates the results so node ids stay injective. 609 /// 610 private static string Sanitize(string id) 611 { 612 var sb = new StringBuilder(id.Length); 613 foreach (char c in id) 614 { 615 bool safe = c is (>= 'a' and <= 'z') or (>= 'A' and <= 'Z') or (>= '0' and <= '9'); 616 sb.Append(safe ? c : '_'); 617 } 618 619 return sb.ToString(); 620 } 621 622 /// 623 /// Wrap a label in double quotes for a Mermaid node and make free-text descriptions safe. 624 /// Mermaid flowchart syntax is line-oriented and renders labels as HTML, so a raw label 625 /// can break the WHOLE diagram. Clean — only the two in-scope files remain. Summary of what was built and verified:

**`src/Guardrails.Cli/Ui/OnTheFlyDiagramObserver.cs`** — a new `IRunObserver` decorator mirroring `OnTheFlyLogSiteObserver`'s shape: `TaskStarting` flips the task's container node to `"running"`, `GuardrailFinished` flips only that specific check's leaf node to `"passed"`/`"failed"`, `TaskFinished` flips the container to a settled status (`"passed"`/`"failed"`/`"needs-human"`, mapped from `TaskOutcome`), and every other event is pure pass-through. The Mermaid source/hash/task-folder-targets are threaded via the constructor (design choice documented in the class summary). Node ids reproduce `MermaidRenderer`'s private sanitize+dedupe algorithm locally. The actual re-render (`WriteDiagram`) is a minimal stub throwing `NotImplementedException` — real implementation is `04-implement-diagram-observer`'s job.

**`tests/Guardrails.Integration.Tests/OnTheFlyDiagramObserverTests.cs`** — 7 test cases (including a 3-case theory) firing events at the decorator directly and asserting on `diagram.html`'s file contents, all rooted under a fresh OS temp directory.

**Root cause of the prior two failures, fixed this attempt:** an unrelated pre-existing test (`RetrySalvageTests.cs`, via `$env:GUARDRAILS_WORKSPACE`) writes `outside.txt`/`src/output.txt` as a side effect when the full suite runs inside a live guardrails-managed worktree — those untracked artifacts aren't part of this task's deliverable, so I deleted them after verification, leaving the diff scoped to exactly the two intended files.

Verified: `dotnet build -c Release` clean (0/0); new test class shows 6 red (`NotImplementedException` from the stub, as intended) + 1 green (pure pass-through); full Core suite 744/746 (2 pre-existing unrelated reds from the already-landed search-box stub); full Integration suite 429/437 (6 mine + 1 pre-existing unrelated red from task 05's wiring test, 1 skipped). No state fragment needed per the task contract.
